scope: W1 and K1 public deterministic implementation

test_observation.note: Passing focused tests did not cover the counterexamples below.

findings.statement: The K1 composer evaluates independent prebuilt payloads, accepts mismatched producer and consumer output hashes, does not propagate STALE to downstream components, bypasses the state boundary, and emits an ad-hoc package rather than the modeling-to-paper contract.

The initial evaluator used any-marker aggregation, trusted candidate diagnostics, omitted required fault injections, and manufactured the G8 package in the harness; its earlier 8/8 observations were invalid and were not persisted.
The common runner did not bind result case_id/input_hash and did not recursively reject nested formal outcomes. This candidate-neutral defect was repaired and covered by fault-injection tests.
Malformed context values still escape as TypeError; W1 also accepts an invalid stage.
Both candidates accept a verified-run decision_id mutation while retaining an artifact hash that does not bind the entire decision record.
Both candidates accept synthetic private_key, refresh_token, and UNC-path probes.
Both candidates accept numeric-string scores; W1 additionally accepts a scored FAILED attempt and untrusted but well-formed freeze hashes.
W1 has no candidate-owned four-component composer and cannot satisfy the frozen end-to-end composition gate.

conclusion: K1 must fail G8 and W1 is not an eligible fallback. The frozen noncompensatory selection rule therefore requires FAST_TRACK_IMPLEMENTATION_BLOCKED unless a permitted repair loop closes every failed gate; both candidate repair budgets are exhausted.
